# allinkl_ddns_user (Resource)

Manages a dynamic DNS login of the all-inkl.com (KAS) account: one host name that a router or script keeps pointed at its current address with the login and password.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# home.example.com follows the address a router reports with this login.
resource "allinkl_ddns_user" "home" {
  zone       = "example.com"
  label      = "home"
  comment    = "at home"
  password   = var.ddns_password
  target_ip  = "203.0.113.4"
  dual_stack = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `comment` (String) Free text describing the login. KAS requires one.
- `label` (String) Host label inside the zone, e.g. `home`. Changing it forces a new login.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password the DDNS client authenticates with. Write-only: drift is not detectable; changing the value updates it. As with all Terraform secrets, the value is stored in the state file.
- `target_ip` (String) Initial IPv4 address of the host. The DDNS client moves it afterwards, so the attribute is not refreshed from KAS; `current_ip` holds the live value. Changing it forces a new login.
- `zone` (String) Zone of the host, e.g. `example.com`. Changing it forces a new login.

### Optional

- `dual_stack` (Boolean) Let the host carry an A and an AAAA record.

### Read-Only

- `current_ip` (String) IPv4 address the host points at now.
- `current_ipv6` (String) IPv6 address the host points at now, in dual-stack mode.
- `host` (String) The full host name, `label.zone`.
- `id` (String) KAS-assigned login, e.g. `dyn0123456`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import allinkl_ddns_user.home dyn0123456
```
